# datum.day

> datum records a life as small timestamped entries (a coffee, a stretch of sleep, where someone is, how they feel)
> and shows them back as timelines and the state of things now. datum.day is the full datum in the browser; each
> record is a SQLite database on the person's own device, synced peer to peer. Open source (AGPL).

AI agents helping someone track their life, or keeping a record of their own, start here:

- [datum.day for AI agents](https://datum.day/agents.md): the four kinds of entry, how to interview your person and
  hand them a setup to paste into datum.day's prompt, syncing with them from the CLI, and keeping your own record.

## Source and docs

- [The repository](https://github.com/vividn/datum): the README, the CLI, and datum.day's source under `web/`
- [docs/agents.md](https://github.com/vividn/datum/blob/main/docs/agents.md): the longer guide for agents
- [skills/datum/SKILL.md](https://github.com/vividn/datum/blob/main/skills/datum/SKILL.md): the CLI skill
- [docs/commands.md](https://github.com/vividn/datum/blob/main/docs/commands.md): every command
